subject.title: [Feature]: Support for sandbox Docker parameters (--gpus all, --ipc=host)

question: Should OpenClaw expose Docker host IPC for agent sandboxes, and if yes should it be a narrow typed break-glass config field instead of generic raw Docker argument passthrough?
rationale: GPU passthrough is already shipped, but the remaining host IPC/raw-args request changes the sandbox isolation boundary and public config contract.

options.title: Add narrow IPC break-glass field
options.body: Expose a typed opt-in IPC setting with schema, docs, config hashing, Docker create args, security audit coverage, warnings, and focused tests while keeping raw Docker args unsupported.

options.title: Reject host IPC in core
options.body: Keep GPU passthrough as the supported high-power Docker path and document that host IPC remains unavailable because it weakens sandbox isolation.

options.title: Define broader namespace policy first
options.body: Pause implementation until maintainers decide one policy for IPC, PID, network namespace joins, capabilities, and other dangerous Docker options.

recommendation.title: Add narrow IPC break-glass field
recommendation.body: Expose a typed opt-in IPC setting with schema, docs, config hashing, Docker create args, security audit coverage, warnings, and focused tests while keeping raw Docker args unsupported.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal is recent sandbox namespace and dangerous Docker override policy work.
